speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; could you please detail your past medical conditions and exactly how your balance and coordination issues have progressed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; the description of looking "drunk" while walking suggests a distinct gait disturbance. To narrow this down, are you experiencing any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right arm or leg? Additionally, do you have a history of stroke, diabetes, or any prior head injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The combination of subacute ataxia, a history of Crohn's disease, and recent treatment with natalizumab (an anti-CD52 monoclonal antibody) is highly suggestive of this opportunistic JC virus infection.
